AfterSideTurnEnd.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): The reset moved to the right slot. Kusarigama.cs's player-side AfterSideTurnEnd is turn_structure step 64, which runs AFTER the hand flush; the port used `on_player_turn_end`, which is Hook.BeforeTurnEnd (step 48) -- about sixteen steps too early. `relics/kusarigama.py` now implements `after_player_turn_end`, the slot whose own docstring names Hook.AfterTurnEnd and distinguishes it from BeforeTurnEnd. The reachability the entry established is what made it matter: the ported StampedePower auto-plays N Attacks from the LATER slot, so the counter was being cleared before those plays could count toward it.  Pinned by test/test_relic_residue_gaps.py.  NOT CLOSED: nothing at this site.  The text it replaced read: WRONG TURN-END SLOT. C#'s player-side AfterSideTurnEnd is audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json step 64 -- it runs AFTER the hand flush -- and the sim HAS that slot: hooks.after_player_turn_end (hooks.py:303-310), whose own docstring says it is Hook.AfterTurnEnd and is 'Distinct from on_player_turn_end, which is Hook.BeforeTurnEnd' (step 48). kusarigama.py:32-33 uses on_player_turn_end, so the reset happens ~16 steps too early. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b08.py b08-kusarigama): the ported StampedePower auto-plays N Attacks from `on_player_turn_end` (powers.py:1023-1039) -- the SAME sim hook -- and its C# home is StampedePower.cs:18 AfterAutoPostPlayPhaseEntered, which turn_structure step 47 places BEFORE step 64. So C# always resets after those Attacks and the sim may not: with Stampede(2) on the player and the executed listener order ['Kusarigama', 'StampedePower'], end_turn leaves _attacks_this_turn=2 where C# leaves 0, and those 2 carry into the next turn -- shifting every 'every 3rd Attack' trigger for the rest of the combat. Both sides ported: Stampede is the Ironclad card cards/stampede.py:36. Bounded, not run-wide: the on_combat_start reset above stops it leaking past the combat. The `participants.Contains(base.Owner.Creature)` filter is structurally satisfied (the sim fires this hook for the player side only). Fix: move the reset to after_player_turn_end, the slot relics/parrying_shield.py:24 already uses. Rule 7: hooks.py, powers.py, cards/stampede.py, relics/parrying_shield.py, src/Core/Models/Powers/StampedePower.cs and audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json are not hashed by this record.

AfterCardPlayed.issue: DORMANT, re-settled round 11 (guard G2 re-derived from today's callers, not trusted from prior prose). NARROWED 2026-07-27. The per-Replay half (G1) is CLOSED: CombatState._resolve_card_play fires on_card_played inside the play-count loop (sts2_rl/combat.py:858-903). WHAT REMAINS is guard G2, the candidate list: Kusarigama.cs picks with `RunState.Rng.CombatTargets.NextItem(HittableEnemies)` and sts2_rl/relics/kusarigama.py:40 still passes `self.living_enemies()` -- and `sts2_rl/relics/base.py` has since grown a dedicated `hittable_enemies()` helper (base.py:449-451, `self.combat.hittable_enemies`) for exactly this C# distinction, which this relic was not updated to use. `living_enemies()` filters on `not e.is_gone` alone (base.py:440-447) -- no Hook.should_allow_hitting term -- so an alive-but-unhittable enemy is still eligible to be drawn. RE-VERIFIED DORMANT: `should_allow_hitting` now has THREE sim implementers (`grep -n 'def should_allow_hitting' sts2_rl/`: powers.py:1908 IllusionPower, powers.py:2780 ReattachPower, powers.py:3905 AdaptablePower -- ReattachPower is new since this guard was first written), and all three gate on `target is self.owner and self.is_reviving`, with `is_reviving` set only from each power's own `on_death` (i.e. after `hp <= 0`). `Creature.is_dead` is a bare `hp <= 0` (creatures.py:47-48) and `is_gone` is `is_dead or escaped` (creatures.py:51-53) with NO carve-out for `retained_after_death` -- so every creature any of the three implementers would refuse to hit is ALREADY `is_gone` and therefore already excluded by `living_enemies()`'s own filter, before `should_allow_hitting` is ever consulted. The mechanism G2 describes (a creature `should_allow_hitting` refuses that is NOT `is_gone`) has no ported instance. Porting a `should_allow_hitting` override that can return False for a creature with `hp > 0` makes it live.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): AfterCardPlayed fires once per Replay iteration in C# but once per play in the sim, so a replayed Attack advances Kusarigama's counter by 1 instead of 2
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the hook bracket is per CardPlay now. CombatState._resolve_card_play opens `for play_index in range(play_count)` and fires `hooks.before_card_played` INSIDE it (sts2_rl/combat.py:574-576) and `hooks.on_card_played` at the end of each iteration, gated on the combat still being in progress (sts2_rl/combat.py:597-600) -- CardModel.cs:1904-1965's `for (int i = 0; i < playCount; i++)` with Hook.BeforeCardPlayed at :1929 and Hook.AfterCardPlayed at :1957-1959. A replayed card therefore fires both hooks once per iteration, as in the game. WAS: combat.py bracketed the WHOLE play-count loop, so a Throwing-Axe-doubled card fired each hook once.

RE-VERIFIED round 11 (the entry was not re-derived, only trusted, at the last pass -- and its cited line numbers had drifted): C# picks the random target from `Enemies.Where(e => e.IsHittable)` (CombatState.cs:142), and IsHittable is `!IsDead && Hook.ShouldAllowHitting(CombatState, this)` (Creature.cs:285-299). Relic.living_enemies() (relics/base.py:440-447) filters on `not e.is_gone` only, and base.py has since grown a dedicated `hittable_enemies()` (base.py:449-451) that kusarigama.py was never switched to. This is the SAME divergence audit/records/relic/bag_of_marbles.json guard G2 records at its own call site, and it carries the same verdict per binding rule 3 -- but it bites harder here, because the set is not just the damage target list, it is the population of an RNG DRAW: `combat_rng.targets.choice(living)` is Rng.NextItem, whose index is scaled by len(seq) (rng.py:248-252), so an unhittable-but-alive enemy changes WHICH enemy is picked even when the pick itself would have been legal, and can also waste the trigger on a target DamageCmd.deal then no-ops on (`should_allow_hitting` returns 0 -- cmds.py:50-51). DORMANT, RE-EXECUTED: `grep -n 'def should_allow_hitting' sts2_rl/` now finds THREE implementers (powers.py:1908 IllusionPower, powers.py:2780 ReattachPower -- new since this guard was first written, powers.py:3905 AdaptablePower), all gating on `target is self.owner and self.is_reviving`, and `is_reviving` is set only from each one's own `on_death`, i.e. after `hp <= 0`. `Creature.is_dead` is `hp <= 0` with no `retained_after_death` carve-out (creatures.py:47-53), so a creature any of the three would refuse to hit is already `is_gone` and already excluded by `living_enemies()` before `should_allow_hitting` is ever asked -- the DORMANT conclusion holds against today's three implementers, not just the original two. Porting any effect that makes a LIVING (hp>0) enemy untargetable makes it live, and in an RNG-visible way (the CombatTargets stream position stays equal but the chosen index diverges). Rule 7: src/Core/Combat/CombatState.cs, src/Core/Entities/Creatures/Creature.cs, relics/base.py, rng.py, cmds.py, creatures.py and powers.py are not hashed by this record.
